claim: Pi describes itself as a minimal terminal coding harness whose features such as sub-agents and plan mode are intentionally not baked in; they can be built as extensions, skills, or packages.
evidence: The README philosophy section says Pi is aggressively extensible, has no built-in sub-agents, and has no built-in plan mode.
relevance: Any Cartographer improvement should be small, explicit, and packaged as skills/tools rather than becoming a heavyweight always-on orchestrator.
title: Pi minimalism favors extension over baked-in workflows

claim: Pi compaction summarizes older messages while preserving recent work, but the docs state compaction is lossy and full history remains only in the session file.
evidence: The compaction docs explicitly say compaction is lossy and summarize older content to free context.
relevance: Cartographer should persist structured phase state outside the chat before compaction is needed.
title: Compaction is useful but lossy

claim: Pi extension docs warn that tools must truncate output because large outputs can cause context overflow, compaction failures, and degraded model performance; built-ins use 50KB/2000-line limits.
evidence: The extension docs state tools MUST truncate output and document 50KB/2000-line defaults.
relevance: Cartographer tools should return compact summaries by default and put full payloads in artifacts.
title: Tool output must be truncated

claim: GrepRAG reports ripgrep retrieval around 0.40s on diffusers versus 3s-7s for baselines, and 1.45s versus >50s on a 754k LOC Java repository.
evidence: The paper reports ripgrep at approximately 0.40s for diffusers and about 1/35th the time cost for FloatingPoint.
relevance: Cartographer should keep `rg`/lexical verification as the default path for exact code evidence.
title: Lexical retrieval can outperform heavier code RAG on latency

claim: GrepRAG identifies high-frequency ambiguous keywords plus context redundancy/fragmentation as key limitations, and improves with identifier-weighted reranking and structure-aware deduplication.
evidence: The paper names keyword ambiguity, redundancy, fragmentation, identifier-weighted re-ranking, and structure-aware deduplication.
relevance: Cartographer context packing should dedupe/merge adjacent snippets and downrank generic terms.
title: GrepRAG failure modes are ambiguity and context fragmentation

claim: Aider sends a concise repository map of important files, classes, functions, signatures, and graph-ranked dependencies within a token budget, with --map-tokens defaulting to about 1k.
evidence: Aider docs say it selects the most relevant repo-map portions using graph ranking and a token budget.
relevance: Cartographer should add a small repo-map/context synopsis instead of feeding raw query JSON or large files.
title: Aider uses compact graph-ranked repo maps

claim: SWE-agent attributes improved results to simple LM-centric commands and feedback formats, including 100-line file viewing, linter-gated edits, and concise search output listing matching files rather than confusing match context.
evidence: SWE-agent docs list a special file viewer, linter on edit, and concise full-directory search output.
relevance: Cartographer should improve tool ergonomics and make failures harder through bounded outputs and safer query/search wrappers.
title: SWE-agent performance depends on ACI design

claim: Anthropic recommends the simplest solution possible, using workflows for predictable code paths and agents only when flexibility is needed; agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance.
evidence: The Building Effective Agents post says to find the simplest solution and only increase complexity when needed.
relevance: Cartographer should default to deterministic parent/tool workflow and escalate only for judgment-heavy tasks.
title: Use simple workflows before autonomous agents

claim: Anthropic reports multi-agent research can outperform single-agent research but uses much more tokens, including about 15x chat-token usage, and notes many coding tasks have fewer truly parallelizable parts.
evidence: The multi-agent research post reports 15x token cost and says most coding tasks involve fewer truly parallelizable tasks than research.
relevance: Cartographer should avoid default subagent fanout and require effort budgets/timeouts/file-only outputs.
title: Multi-agent research is costly and best for parallel breadth

claim: Claude Code best practices state that context fills quickly with conversation, files, and command output; performance degrades as it fills, so users should clear/compact and use subagents for bounded investigation.
evidence: The docs say context is the most important resource to manage and recommend /clear, /compact, and scoped subagents.
relevance: Cartographer should enforce context budgets and phase handoff summaries.
title: Context window is the resource to manage

claim: OpenAI Codex best practices recommend prompts include goal, context, constraints, and done-when; complex tasks should plan first and use AGENTS.md/skills for durable workflow guidance.
evidence: Codex docs list Goal, Context, Constraints, and Done when as a good default prompt structure.
relevance: Cartographer plan/implementation prompts should carry concise acceptance contracts instead of long prose.
title: Codex recommends scoped prompts and done criteria

claim: LangGraph checkpointers enable inspection, interruption, approval, and resuming graph state after human updates.
evidence: Context7 LangGraph docs show StateGraph compiled with a checkpointer and human interrupt/resume examples.
relevance: Cartographer can mimic this minimally with filesystem checkpoints and phase status files, without adopting LangGraph.
title: Durable checkpoints support resumable workflows

claim: LlamaIndex provides TransformRetriever/query transforms and exposes retrieved source_nodes for contexts and evaluation.
evidence: Context7 LlamaIndex snippets show query transforms before retrieval and collecting response.source_nodes.
relevance: Cartographer should log query expansions/misses and keep source-backed context references.
title: Query transforms and source nodes support disciplined retrieval

claim: DSPy optimizers tune LM programs against metrics using a program, a metric, and a small training set, rather than relying only on manual prompt tweaking.
evidence: Context7 DSPy docs describe optimizers taking a program, metric, and training inputs.
relevance: Cartographer should measure success-per-token and validation pass rate from real sessions before adding complexity.
title: Prompt/workflow optimization should be metric-driven

claim: The dogfooding session had 607 JSONL entries, 288 assistant messages, 287 tool results, 37.6M cache-read tokens, and one compaction at 262,950 tokens.
evidence: The generated session analysis records these counts and compaction metadata.
relevance: Workflow changes should prioritize context hygiene and persisted state over chat growth.
title: Dogfooding session hit context bloat

claim: The largest dogfooding outputs included 63,793 and 52,484 character `cartographer_index query` results, 51KB diff/rg outputs, and a 32,945 character web extract.
evidence: Session analysis largest-output table lists these payloads.
relevance: Cartographer tools should default to concise `context`/summaries and save full outputs to files.
title: Large tool outputs polluted the session

claim: Dogfooding reviewer and worker subagent calls timed out at 60s, 90s, and 120s; deterministic validation was still used to move forward.
evidence: Session analysis subagent outcomes list reviewer/worker timeout results.
relevance: Subagents should be optional, bounded, and replaced by deterministic validators when validation is mechanical.
title: Subagent timeouts slowed work

claim: The `implement the plan` and `continue implementation` turns lasted about 775s and 721s, used 55 and 85 tools, and emitted over 144KB and 192KB of tool text.
evidence: Session analysis longest-turn table records these durations, tool counts, and output sizes.
relevance: Implementation workflow needs phase receipts, targeted checks, and automatic compaction checkpoints.
title: Implementation turns dominated wall time

claim: The project README says `.plan/<topic>` artifacts are intentional rationale to review/commit, while `.plan/_index/` is a generated local SQLite/FTS cache that should not be committed.
evidence: README sections What gets written, JSONL graph artifacts, Retrieval scopes, and Artifact lifecycle document this split.
relevance: The next improvement should refine context budget mechanics rather than changing artifact philosophy.
title: Current Cartographer already separates durable rationale and generated index

claim: Proposal/plan/implement skills already advise against large reads, raw outputs, broad scouting, and child output inlining, but dogfooding still produced large outputs and timeout-prone handoffs.
evidence: Skill delegation guidance includes these rules; session analysis shows they were insufficiently enforced by tools/workflow gates.
relevance: Move key context-budget rules from prose into tool defaults, validators, and receipts.
title: Current skill guidance is advisory but not enforced
